ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, board members, authorized signatories and counterparties against (i) the SECO embargo and sanctions list maintained under the Embargo Act (SR 946.2), (ii) consolidated UN Security Council sanctions, (iii) the EU sanctions regime as adopted autonomously by Switzerland, and (iv) the OFAC SDN List whenever USD clearing, US persons or US-market operations are involved; Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) must be identified pursuant to Art. 3 lit. c AMLA and receive enhanced due diligence consistent with FINMA Circular 2011/01; documented screen results must be archived in the client KYC file for at least ten years; any positive hit triggers refusal of engagement or enhanced verification and, where applicable, immediate filing with the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix — Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex) operated by the Federal Office of Justice (BJ) in conjunction with the cantonal commercial register offices (Handelsregisteramt)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names of a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft may be drafted in German, French, Italian, Rhaeto-Romanic or a foreign language written in Latin script; non-Latin scripts (including Chinese characters) are not accepted and must be transliterated into Latin script; the name must be truthful, clear, non-misleading and capable of serving as a trade name within the meaning of Art. 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; the statutory legal form suffix must be 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (or, for French/Italian linguistic regions, 'Société Anonyme'/'SA' or 'Società Anonima'/'SA'); for an AG registered in a German-speaking canton such as Zug or Zurich, 'AG' is the standard and determinative suffix.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Helvetia (with Swiss cross or federal coat of arms)
Any cantonal or communal geographical denomination (e.g., 'Zürich', 'Luzern', 'Genève') without a genuine local connection
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the cantonal commercial register office rejects or objects to the proposed name, the applicant may file a formal written objection-or-appeal (Beschwerde) with the competent cantonal supervisory authority (e.g., Cantonal Department of Justice or the cantonal administrative court) within thirty days of the rejection order, attaching the rejection decision, the initial name reservation application, and comparable-name search evidence from Zefix; the appeal should propose an alternative compliant name in the alternative; a subsequent appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court in St. Gallen and, thereafter, to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne, each subject to thirty-day filing deadlines; third parties may also oppose a published name within ten days of publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional acceptance. Swiss corporate law (Art. 637 CO) requires that the registered office be the place from which the company is actually managed and administered. A bare mail-forwarding virtual office without a physical administrative seat is rejected by cantonal commercial register offices and by the Federal Tax Administration in substance assessments. For a license-free low-risk micro-SaaS entity operating through merchant of record payment rails (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy), a serviced physical office arrangement such as a co-working space with a dedicated desk, meeting room, mail processing and a locally resident board member is permitted and constitutes sufficient commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk of approximately 3-5% in the first operating year; unannounced physical inspections are not a standard practice for a license-free low-risk Aktiengesellschaft, but the probability increases during tax audits, substance reviews, or automatic exchange of information (AEOI) procedures, and if the company becomes VAT-registered in Switzerland with substantial turnover or commences regulated activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR) Art. 620 et seq.; Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (VKR/HRAO); OR Art. 626, 627, 632, 640, 718, 726.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Directorate of Commercial Registration of the Canton of Registration, connected via the Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zefix); final filing with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Articles of Association (Statuten) together with Commercial Register Application Form (Anmeldung) and supporting notarial minutes of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; minimum paid-up CHF 50,000 (at least 20% of nominal value per share); full capital must be available as a blocked escrow deposit in a Swiss bank, confirmed by the bank's escrow certificate before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The articles of association dated [date] are adopted and the share subscription and full or partial paid-up capital within the legal minimum are ratified; (2) The registered office is established at [street, city, Switzerland]; (3) The fully paid-up capital is confirmed as deposited in an escrow account at [bank name, branch]; (4) The following individuals are elected as directors and officers: [names and functions]; (5) The board is directed to file the incorporation application with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office and to fulfil all notices, legal publications, and declarations under tax and social security law; (6) All prior preparatory acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public qualified in the canton of registration (or the official notarial office, depending on canton).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the German or French language Articles of Association per mandatory OR content (corporate name, seat, purpose, share capital, share categories, board structure, auditors, notices). Schedule a notarial hearing; all founders must personally appear or validly represent; execute the deed of incorporation including the declaration of share subscription and capital contribution plan. Verify that the board members have accepted office. After notarial act, the notary will transmit the certified deed to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Founders' list with names, addresses, and share subscriptions
Declaration of representation if a founder is a legal entity
Bank escrow certificate confirming blocked Swiss bank account in the company's name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry queries missing documents, correct the deficiency within 20 days by filing supplementary notarial declarations or an updated escrow letter; a rejection can be appealed to the cantonal supervisory authority under VKR Art. 35.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Blocked Bank Escrow Account and Paid-up Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or Geneva-licensed financial institution (MIFID/stock exchange member preferred).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the AG (or provisional account in formation). Transfer the required paid-up capital (minimum CHF 50,000) from the founders' accounts by means of a traceable banking transfer. Instruct the bank to issue a formal escrow confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bescheinigung) addressed to the Commercial Register Office, stating the account holder, block condition, and amount available. The escrow must be released only upon presentation of the Commercial Register certificate.
required_dossiers: Excerpt of underlying founders' identification (passport/ID, beneficial ownership for CDB 20)
Completed bank's client onboarding forms (Form A/B)
Source of funds declaration for capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the escrow certificate due to compliance doubts, provide enhanced source-of-funds documentation and audited financial statements of the funding parent entity; apply to a second Swiss bank if administrative refusal persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Application and Legal Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the seat canton; coordinated via Zefix / the e-SUMO online portal of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed and the registration application through the electronic procedure (e-SUMO or the cantonal portal). Sign the application by all board members (electronic qualified signature ETS accepted). The registry reviews the company name for distinctiveness and compliance with the Swiss Trademark Act. Upon approval, the registry sends the petition for publication to the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB). The legal entity is established only after the entry is made in the Commercial Register; SHAB publication is constitutive for third-party effectiveness.
required_dossiers: Notarised articles of association and incorporation minutes
Declarations of acceptance of office by directors
Power-of-attorney if a lawyer submits on behalf
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a deficiency (e.g., name conflict, missing capital proof), reply within the 10-day plea period by supplying corrected articles or an updated notarial addendum. If the registry refuses, an administrative court appeal may be filed within 30 days in accordance with Art. 35 VKR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Social Security and Municipal Trade Licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (e.g., Zurich Steueramt) / Federal Tax Administration (ESTV); Swiss Compensation Office (SVA / Ausgleichskasse); local municipality's business licensing department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Commercial Register excerpt, apply automatically or separately for the VAT number (MWST-Nr.), the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), and the employer registration for social security (AHV/IV/EO). Complete the cantonal taxation questionnaire (Bogen). If physical office premises exist, register the business activity with the local municipality for the occupancy and fire safety control. For a software-only SaaS without physical production, no further industrial license is required, but an occupational safety declaration under SUVA must be filed if employees are hired.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or reference notice for registered office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the cantonal tax authority demands corrective declarations, submit a revised revenue forecast and full cooperation; late fees can be waived if the entity provides evidence that the omission is not willful.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure cloud-based software activities under ISIC 6201; if office conversion or server hardware is installed, the cantonal trade inspectorate and the local municipal office for construction/occupancy are the competent bodies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for micro-SaaS without physical goods or regulated software; only a general Swiss trade/business registration (

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN, BAFU) in cooperation with the cantonal environmental protection authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA (Annex 90 of EIA Ordinance); no environmental permit required for software operation; if the company uses an ordinary service office, it stays in the 'registration-only' low-tier category and merely must comply with local waste ordinances.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No waste-water discharge, VOC emissions, or process emissions from software development; applicable thresholds are de minimis: compliance with Federal Water Protection Act (GSchG) for ordinary sewage from office toilets; separate disposal of electronics under WEEE Ordinance; if a dedicated server room is used, compliance with the EU-VO/CLP labelling and cooling agent handling might be requested.

stage_2.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire brigade (Feuerpolizei) for the registered office and server room if present; structural load inspection of floor slabs if rack-mounted servers are installed; workplace clearance certificate issued by the cantonal labour inspectorate under Art. 82 of the Labour Act (ArG), including electrical installation check and first-aid equipment provision.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Federal Tax Administration FTA); official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; cantonal tax authorities administer direct cantonal and communal corporate taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of a Swiss AG, the cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt) assigns a Swiss Business Identification Number (UID), which serves as the statutory company identifier. VAT registration with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration is required if taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; the VAT UID is obtained by submitting the VAT registration form (Form 500) through the ESTV e-portal. Foreign entities not resident in Switzerland that have no commercial register entry must file Form 500, appoint a Swiss VAT representative (Art. 66 VAT Act) if not using the simplified non-established supplier procedure, and obtain a Swiss VAT UID for supplies made in Switzerland. A non-resident foreign corporation with a Swiss permanent establishment must also register with the cantonal tax authority for income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. A Swiss AG is mandatorily taxed at entity level under Swiss federal and cantonal law. Available statutory elections include: (i) profit and loss transfer agreement with a Swiss resident group company (tax grouping / Organschaft) for corporate income tax, requiring 90% direct or indirect participation and a five-year minimum term; (ii) Swiss VAT grouping (Mehrwertsteuergruppe) for closely held Swiss entities; and (iii) declaration of Swiss capital contribution reserves by the AG to repatriate reserves tax-free. Hybrid mismatch rules follow BEPS Action 2 under Swiss tax law; no elective pass-through classification is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 (exclusive of VAT) of taxable supplies performed in or from Switzerland within a calendar year. For non-established foreign suppliers without a Swiss residence or permanent establishment, the same CHF 100,000 Swiss-turnover threshold applies (Art. 10 para. 2 VAT Act). Optional registration is permitted for turnover below CHF 100,000 (Art. 10 para. 3). In the context of Micro-SaaS via a merchant of record, the platform may already collect and remit Swiss VAT as deemed seller, rendering separate registration unnecessary.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoicing, or digital stamping for VAT. Paper and electronic invoices are accepted if they satisfy the mandatory content requirements of Art. 26 VAT Act. Since 30 June 2020, the Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) standard applies to domestic payment slips, replacing ISR/bank references. There is no tax-authority pre-approval or TDUT data upload requirement. For B2C electronic supplies such as SaaS subscriptions, simplified invoices are permitted. Foreign suppliers using a merchant of record may rely on invoices generated by that platform; neither PIN cryptographic stamps nor solution-provider certification is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: physical export from Swiss territory to a foreign destination qualifies for zero-rating (exemption with input VAT credit) provided the supplier proves exportation through a Swiss customs export declaration. Services: a service supplied by a Swiss provider is outside Swiss VAT scope if the recipient is an enterprise with its domicile or effective place of management abroad (place-of-supply rule under Art. 8 VAT Act); B2C electronic services are treated as supplied at the consumer's place of residence, and Swiss VAT is not chargeable when the consumer is located abroad. For Micro-SaaS export subscriptions, the supplier must maintain evidence that each customer is resident or established outside Switzerland, such as billing address, IP address, payment gateway metadata, and merchant-of-record contract terms, to qualify for effective 0% VAT treatment and preserve input VAT deduction on Swiss costs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (NCTS/e-dec) for physical goods exports
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR (or equivalent carrier document) evidencing physical transport to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank confirmation evidencing foreign-currency repatriation of export proceeds from the overseas customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss tax and customs authorities may retrospectively audit export zero-rating claims; the statutory assessment period is generally five years, extended to ten years in cases of intentional tax evasion (Art. 17 Tax Administrative Procedure Act). If export documentation is found missing, false, or insufficient, the supplies are recharacterised as taxable in Switzerland and VAT is assessed at the standard rate plus default interest and a late-payment penalty. Intentional issuance or use of false export declarations, invoices, or proof-of-export documents constitutes tax evasion under Art. 70 VAT Act, punishable by a fine of up to three times the VAT evaded, and may additionally trigger criminal sanctions under Swiss customs law. Retroactive clawback also applies to input VAT deductions claimed against zero-rated export proceeds where the underlying export evidence fails audit verification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) – Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under the Federal Act on Currency and Means of Payment and the Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank. No exchange controls, no repatriation restrictions, no licensing requirements for profit remittance or capital outflows. Dividend remittances are subject only to statutory Swiss withholding tax at 35% (reduced by applicable double tax treaties to typically 5%–15% upon proper substance documentation). A Swiss AG conducting consumer micro-SaaS may freely invoice global customers and retain/convert export receipts in any convertible currency. The only compliance duties arise under tax law, AML/KYC obligations imposed by FINMA-regulated banks, and SNB statistical reporting for payments exceeding CHF 10,000 or CHF 50,000 depending on instrument type.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation deadline for export receivables. A Swiss exporter may hold foreign currency indefinitely in a Swiss or offshore account, provided the balance is disclosed for Swiss tax (accounting) purposes and, if applicable, for SNB reportable payment statistics. For VAT and customs purposes, no FX conversion obligation arises; the tax authorities apply monthly Swiss Franc reference rates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Freigabekonto) for share capital payment; subsequently Operational Corporate Account
Capital Escrow Account; Operational Corporate Account with multi-currency and SEPA capability
Operational Corporate Account; Capital Escrow Account under cooperative bank rules

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse (Schweiz) AG, now integrated into UBS Group
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account; Operational Corporate Account for wealth-linked banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium legal viability for the Swiss micro-SaaS treasury, but not as a substitute for a FINMA-licensed bank. Switzerland is not an EEA member, so the PSD2 Single Passport is unavailable. An offshore EMI (e.g. Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) can provide disbursement rails and currency conversion, but holding Swiss client funds or providing banking-type deposit services in Switzerland requires a Swiss banking license or a fintech authorization under Art. 1b Banking Act. For the Swiss AG’s own treasury, an offshore EMI may serve as a payment collection gateway for SaaS subscriptions (e.g. Paddle, Lemon Squeezy), but the primary operating account should remain with a Swiss bank to ensure legal certainty, substance, and FINMA-supervised asset segregation. Non-bank EMIs also face stricter due diligence on inbound founder capital injections due to opaqueness.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a domestic Swiss AG, physical board appearance is generally not statutorily mandated for account opening. FINMA anti-money-laundering rules permit identity verification by video identification, SwissID, or qualified electronic signature provided the bank has a compliant onboarding process. In practice, Tier-1 traditional banks often require an authorised signatory (director or person with sole signature) to attend at least one initial meeting in person at a Swiss branch or at a Swiss embassy/consulate abroad. Remote opening is accepted by Swiss fintech banks and some cantonal banks for low-risk corporate entities, provided the UBO declaration and corporate documents are certified. Private banks may impose stricter physical interview requirements for non-resident directors. A robust compliance posture is to schedule an in-person interview with the beneficial owner and signatory in Zurich or Zug to eliminate cross-border onboarding friction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership: natural-person UBO not clearly identified due to layered structure or nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Attested UBO declaration per Swiss Code of Obligations; valid passport or national ID of all UBOs; extract of the commercial register not older than 90 days; notarised Articles of Association; corporate chart for holding chain; Swiss tax/anti-money-laundering Form A signed by UBO; references from existing bank or legal counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection sourced from cryptocurrency exchange proceeds, high volatility or unregulated platform.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-certified withdrawal history from regulated exchange (FINMA or equivalent); blockchain transaction analyses for source of cryptocurrency; personal tax audit statement or tax clearance confirming previous gains; details of wallet ownership; contract or invoice explaining the disposition of tokens; director/UBO net-worth statement and source-of-wealth explanation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors or UBOs resident in FATF high-risk jurisdictions, or existence of PEP (politically exposed person) status without disclosure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Explanation of professional nexus to Switzerland; employer verification letter; passport and proof of address; PEP declaration form confirming or denying PEP status; documentation of the source of wealth and source of funds; confirmation that funds originate from transparent regulated sources; Swiss tax compliance certificate or foreign residency certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Swiss AG minimum capital of CHF 100,000 (immediately 100% paid) or simplified CHF 20,000 with the payroll trust exception, the founder/shareholder transfers the capital via SWIFT MT103 for international currencies or SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for domestic CHF. The remittance should identify the beneficiary as the not-yet-incorporated company or the established AG with the escrow account reference. The bank opens a 'Freigabekonto' (escrow account) in the AG’s name with a restricted instruction until the commercial register confirms incorporation. The MT103 remittance information field (Field 70) should state 'SACHEINLAGE/APPORT EN NATURE/EINZAHLUNG' or 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' to avoid misclassification. No central bank approval or official purpose code is required under Swiss law; for statistical balance-of-payments reporting, the bank captures the code 'Capital investment – share capital' if so instructed. The commercial register office requires a bank confirmation that the fully paid-up share capital is at the free disposal of the board before issuing the registration certificate. Source of funds verification is conducted in accordance with the Anti-Money-Laundering Ordinance and the bank’s risk-based due diligence manual.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements the Swiss AG uses the following clearing rails: 1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for international high-valiue CHF, USD, EUR or other convertible currencies, with beneficiary bank details and purpose of payment (e.g. software license, cloud hosting); 2) SEPA Credit Transfers for EUR-denominated payments to EEA counterparts (Sorbet clears via EACH, with the Swiss AG as participant); 3) SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) instant and batch systems for domestic CHF; 4) API-based payment platforms (e.g. Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) for merchant settlement and franchise royalties; 5) Commercial letters of credit are disproportionately rare for SaaS transactions; they apply only if the counterparty requires an underlying goods transaction, while artistic and software licensing is invoiced under service contracts with SWIFT or SEPA rails. Export proceeds can be collected into a Swiss multi-currency account or an EMI, with no mandatory conversion to CHF.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter (OTC) forward contracts (plain-vanilla FX forwards) with a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank
FX options (European-style and barrier options) for underwriting subscription margins
Cross-currency swaps for converting foreign-currency debt or operating leases into CHF
Exchange-traded FX futures and options on Eurex or CME for covered positions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for exotic restricted currencies (e.g. KRW, INR) governed by ISDA 1998 FX and Currency Option Definitions
Short-term FX brokers through multi-bank platforms (EBS, Reuters) under enforceable UK or Swiss law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convening and holding of the annual shareholders' meeting (Generalversammlung) with board approvals of financial statements, share register, and applicable audit waiver resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal shareholders' resolution; no filing with the Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the balance sheet date, i.e., no later than 30 June for a 31 December year-end (Art. 699 Code of Obligations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors become personally liable for damages; a shareholder may petition a court to convene the meeting; repeated failure to constitute statutory organs triggers the Commercial Register's administrative strike-off procedure under Art. 731b CO with prior publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and cantonal corporate income tax return (Steuererklärung / Déclaration fiscale) for direct federal tax, cantonal/municipal profit tax, and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration (e.g., Zug/Zurich) and the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) for the direct federal tax share
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, the return is ordinarily due by 31 March of the following year; cantonal practice commonly grants an extension to end of September upon application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A reminder (Mahnung) is issued after 30 days, default interest at 4.0–4.5% p.a. accrues on assessed amounts, and cantonal administrative fines (Ordnungsbusse) up to CHF 10,000 may be imposed; continued non-filing leads to ex officio assessment, enforced collection, and possible dissolution of the company by the competent authority under Art. 731b CO.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT settlement and return (Mehrwertsteuer-Abrechnung) for supplies of digital SaaS services including zero-rated export supplies and input VAT recovery claims
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) via the Swiss VAT e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the settlement period; for a 31 December yearly settlement, the return is due by early March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing contravention fines up to CHF 5,000 under Art. 87 VAT Act, late-payment interest at 4.0% p.a. from the due date, repayment of improperly offset input VAT; prolonged defaults may result in cancellation of VAT registration and posting of security guarantees, but no direct company strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audit waiver declaration (Verzicht auf die eingeschränkte Revision) by unanimous shareholders' resolution or appointment of an independent statutory auditor if the waiver conditions are not met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting minutes; no filing to the Commercial Register unless appointment of an auditor must be notified
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Resolution adopted at the annual shareholders' meeting held within 6 months of the balance sheet date, effective immediately and valid for the completed and following fiscal year (Art. 727a CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A waiver adopted in breach of Art. 727a CO (e.g., average annual workforce above 10 full-time positions or a shareholder holding ≥10% of capital demanding an audit) is void; the court may order the appointment of an auditor upon petition, and absence of a required auditor may lead to Commercial Register enforcement and director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit (ordentliche Revision) is mandatory if the company exceeds two of the following thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets of CHF 20 million, annual turnover of CHF 40 million, and an annual average of 250 full-time employees (Art. 727 CO). Below these thresholds, a limited audit (eingeschränkte Revision) is required unless unanimously waived by the shareholders; such waiver is impermissible if the company exceeds 10 average full-time employees per year or if a shareholder holding at least 10% of the share capital requests an auditor appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations statutory accounts (Rechnungslegung nach Art. 957–963b OR) under Swiss minimum accounting standards; voluntary application of Swiss GAAP FER (Fachempfehlungen zur Rechnungslegung) permitted and recommended for transparency; IFRS required only for listed companies or where mandated by the board or auditor

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no standalone annual UBO (ultimate beneficial owner) confirmation or declaration filing for private stock companies. The company must maintain an accurate register of shareholders (Aktienbuch) recording legal name, domicile, and citizenship of each registered shareholder with acquisition dates (Art. 686 CO); any transfer of registered shares is effective only upon entry in the register, and the board is obliged to update the register within the annual cycle and approve it at the AGM. Bearer shares are prohibited for non-listed companies and must be converted into registered shares. For tax filing purposes, shareholding details of shareholders are declared in the cantonal tax return as at the assessment date, and any transfers of participations remain recordable in the Aktienbuch.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Verwaltungsrat minutes and election resolutions)
Minute Book (Board and General Meeting minutes)
Accounting records, vouchers, and annual financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,900 – 5,700 (CHF 1,600 – 4,800) per annum covering registered office provision, statutory correspondence handling in Zurich or Zug, mailbox services, and basic corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 – 4,000 (CHF 1,000 – 3,400) for the annual limited audit confirmation or audit waiver formalities; a full ordinary statutory audit for a micro-SaaS exceeding thresholds typically ranges USD 5,000 – 18,000 (CHF 4,500 – 15,500) depending on complexity and audit firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory corporate income tax rate is 8.5% (effective federal burden approximately 7.83% because cantonal taxes are deductible). Combined federal, cantonal and communal headline effective rate in Canton Zug is approximately 14.6%–15.1%, depending on the commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No federal tax holiday is available under general law. Under the Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing Act (TRAF), cantons may grant a patent box exemption on qualifying IP income (up to 90% profit exemption) and an additional R&D deduction of up to 50% of qualifying R&D expenditure. These incentives are not automatic for a consumer micro-SaaS business and require qualifying Swiss software/patent innovation and cantonal implementation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal combined federal/cantonal corporate income tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung juristische Personen), filed through the canton's electronic filing system; software-supported transmission via SwissTax-compatible platforms is accepted by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration and the Canton Zug Tax Administration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for each fiscal year; no quarterly corporate income tax returns are prescribed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year corporate taxpayers the return is generally due by 31 March of the following year; where prepared by a licensed Swiss tax adviser, the deadline is commonly extended to 30 June or a later date granted by the cantonal tax administration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, UID/IDE number, domicile, date of incorporation, the share capital and legal form (Aktiengesellschaft).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Swiss UID/IDE of the AG and supply the ownership annex identifying all non-resident shareholders. No personal residence details of shareholders are required on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code and description; for the target entity use ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 lightweight productivity cloud software operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark 'ordinary taxation with no special status' unless a cantonal patent-box ruling was granted for qualifying software IP. Non-resident management positions do not change the activity description.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide gross revenue from SaaS subscriptions, software licenses, maintenance fees and ancillary services in Swiss francs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross receipts before payment-processor fees even if revenue is collected through Paddle or Lemon Squeezy. Foreign-currency revenue must be converted at the average annual rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs including cloud hosting, software development, employee salaries, marketing, legal fees, payment processing fees and intercompany charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only arm's-length intercompany costs are deductible; related-party royalties and service charges must be supported by transfer pricing documentation. Payments to non-residents should be reviewed for Swiss withholding tax exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statement profit adjusted for non-deductible expenses, tax-deductible reserves, loss carryforwards, IP box relief and R&D deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Swiss GAAP or a recognized equivalent; attach the balance sheet and income statement. Foreign-source losses are not available if the double taxation treaty assigns the right of taxation to the foreign state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Anticipatory tax credits for Swiss dividends, Swiss bank interest and qualifying foreign taxes underlying the profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Swiss-resident taxpayer can claim the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax credit. Non-resident shareholders invoke the applicable DTA refund procedure separately and cannot use this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - Related-party transactions / transfer pricing annex
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with related parties: loans, IP licences, SaaS reseller arrangements, payment rail contracts and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Name the non-resident parent or affiliated counterparty; attach the local file, master file and any APA/ruling if the tax administration requests it.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a written reminder, a cantonal procedural surcharge and, if refusal continues, discretionary tax assessment. Federal procedural fines may reach CHF 10,000. Interest runs on unpaid tax at approximately 3% per annum. Intentional tax evasion carries a statutory fine of up to 200% of the tax evaded; fraudulent falsification of documents constitutes tax fraud and may lead to imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) applies to dividend distributions. Under tax treaties the rate may be reduced, typically to 5% for a foreign corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the voting capital and to 15% for portfolio holdings; some DTAs provide 0%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must apply to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for a full or partial refund of the 35% anticipatory tax using the official DTA refund form. The application must be accompanied by a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, a beneficial ownership declaration, documentary evidence of shareholding on the distribution date and confirmation that the shareholder qualifies for treaty protection. Relief at source may be granted only after ESTV approval; otherwise the tax is withheld and then refunded.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Switzerland does not impose a general withholding tax on arm's-length outbound royalties or ordinary trade interest paid to non-residents. However, 35% anticipatory tax applies to interest on Swiss-issued bonds, money-market instruments and certain bank interest; most Swiss tax treaties reduce such interest withholding to 0% or 10%. No statutory Swiss withholding tax applies to pure SaaS licence royalty payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF: No fixed statutory CHF threshold obliges a company to file a Local File or Master File with the annual tax return. Documentation must be produced upon request where cross-border related-party transactions are material. A Country-by-Country report is mandatory in Switzerland for any Swiss-resident ultimate parent entity with consolidated group revenue of at least CHF 900 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply offshore Economic Substance Regulations. Swiss anti-abuse and treaty-entitlement rules nevertheless require genuine economic substance: a registered office, physical premises, effective management decisions, personnel, books and records in Switzerland. A letterbox AG is treated as lacking substance, may be denied treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test and may be disregarded or reconstructed as the foreign shareholder's Swiss permanent establishment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and tax fraud (Steuerhinterziehung / Steuerbetrug)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting Swiss SaaS subscription revenue, overstating deductible payments to foreign related parties, or submitting falsified financial statements to reduce the corporate income tax assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: For direct federal tax, an evasion penalty of up to 200% of the evaded tax plus interest; for tax fraud using forged evidence, a prison term of up to three years or a fine. Cantonal tax law imposes analogous fines and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in or approve the fraudulent return may be jointly and severally liable; intentional manipulation of corporate separation can pierce the corporate veil, exposing personal assets. Criminal convictions may trigger travel restrictions and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an Aktiengesellschaft in Zug with no Swiss office, employees, business records, or management decisions, using the Swiss registration only to obtain treaty benefits or perceived reputational status while all SaaS activity is controlled from abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the Swiss company as a permanent establishment of the foreign owner; denial of Swiss tax treaty benefits; deemed distribution of accumulated profits subject to 35% anticipatory tax; added tax and penalty surcharges; potential administrative dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the company is held to be a façade, shareholders and directors can be personally liable for corporate tax and creditor claims. Directors may also face disqualification orders and cantonal fines for false statutory declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the micro-SaaS entity as an uninvoiced pass-through for customer funds collected via payment aggregators, concealing beneficial ownership, or issuing fictitious SaaS invoices to move value to high-risk jurisdictions without suspicious transaction reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Penal Code, money laundering (Art. 305bis) is punishable by up to three years' imprisonment or a fine; aggravated money laundering (Art. 305ter) carries up to five years' imprisonment plus fines of up to CHF 500,000. Assets are subject to confiscation and freezing orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and compliance officers face direct criminal liability, including imprisonment and personal fines. Assets of directors may be seized and international travel bans imposed while the criminal investigation is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing mispricing and unlawful profit extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling SaaS subscriptions or IP licences to a non-resident affiliate at margins below arm's length, paying excessive royalties to a low-tax jurisdiction for dormant code, or failing to maintain intercompany agreements and pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward tax assessment based on the arm's-length principle, compensatory interest, reclassification of the price difference as a constructive dividend subject to 35% anticipatory tax, plus penalty surcharges of up to 200% of the additional tax found.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute artificial pricing and do not ensure withholding of the Swiss anticipatory tax may be held personally liable for the withheld-but-unpaid tax. Criminal tax-fraud prosecutions may result in imprisonment and director disqualification.
